themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters spiked to 13 complaints THIS WEEK, up 352% from the 8-week baseline average of 2.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 8.68), signaling a sudden emergence of public safety or quality-of-life enforcement issues that warrant investigation into whether a specific incident cluster or enforcement pattern is driving the spike.
evidence: 13 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (352% spike)
Z-score of 8.68 indicates extreme statistical deviation
Spike is brand-new (this week only) with no prior escalation in recent weeks
reporting_angles: Report on what specific non-emergency incidents are driving the spike—are complaints concentrated in one neighborhood pocket, or spread across Midwood/Ocean Parkway?
Interview NYPD precinct commander and residents to understand whether enforcement has intensified or if residents are newly filing complaints in response to a specific incident

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 36 THIS WEEK, up 164% from the 8-week average of 13.6 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.2), suggesting rapid pavement degradation, pothole formation, or infrastructure failure concentrated in the past 7 days.
evidence: 36 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.6 weekly average (164% increase)
Z-score of 5.2 indicates statistically significant deviation
281 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (214 alterations, 23 new buildings) suggest active construction that may be damaging streets
reporting_angles: Map the geographic distribution of complaints—are potholes and damaged conditions clustered around specific construction sites or major intersections?
Determine whether DOB permits for alterations or new buildings are correlated with street damage complaints; interview NYC Department of Transportation about repair timeline

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 22 THIS WEEK, up 340% from the 8-week baseline of 5.0 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.01), indicating a sudden garbage collection failure, sanitation service gap, or illegal dumping outbreak affecting household waste management.
evidence: 22 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.0 weekly average (340% spike)
Z-score of 5.01 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Unsanitary conditions (924 complaints over 90 days) and dirty condition complaints (474) remain elevated, suggesting broader sanitation dysfunction
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to identify whether a collection route was missed, rerouted, or suspended this week in Midwood/Ocean Parkway
Interview residents about whether garbage is piling up on curbs, collection frequency has dropped, or illegal dumping has increased; photograph affected blocks

themes_detail.label: Illegal Animal Pet Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Illegal animal kept as pet complaints skyrocketed 2,300% with 3 complaints 2 weeks ago versus 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69), suggesting an emerging exotic pet or livestock-keeping problem in a residential area, though the small absolute volume and prior low baseline warrant verification of whether this reflects a real problem or reporting artifact.
evidence: 3 illegal animal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% percentage increase)
Z-score of 8.69 is highest among all spikes, though absolute complaint volume is very low
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago and may have already subsided; requires confirmation of whether complaints continue
reporting_angles: Verify the type of animals involved and their locations—are complaints concentrated on a single block, or spread throughout the district?

Interview Animal Care & Control to determine whether they've received corresponding service requests and what enforcement actions have been taken; identify whether residents are reporting exotic pets, roosters, or other animals

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal & Street Sign Infrastructure Failure
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal complaints surged 2 weeks ago to 138, up 323% from the 8-week average of 32.6 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.5), and street sign damage hit 5 complaints (900% increase from 0.5 avg), suggesting coordinated infrastructure failure from weather, construction, or deferred maintenance affecting traffic safety.
evidence: 138 traffic signal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 32.6 weekly average (323% spike, z-score: 6.5)
5 street sign damage complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (900% spike, z-score: 6.36)
Both spikes occurred in the same week, suggesting systemic infrastructure event rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Investigate whether a weather event, storm, or power outage 2-3 weeks ago caused widespread signal and sign failures in Midwood/Ocean Parkway
Request NYC Department of Transportation repair status on outstanding traffic signal complaints; identify whether backlog exists and how long repairs typically take
